Ensuring veterans receive top-tier cancer care through qualified medical physicists at the VA is critical, but H.R. 3489's cosponsor list raises eyebrows—13 Democrats vs. 1 Republican. While standardizing roles for these specialists could improve treatment accuracy, the bill's partisan tilt risks embedding bureaucratic bloat rather than streamlining care.

The VA's track record of wasting $369M on failed IT systems (2023 OIG report) demands strict oversight to prevent similar misuse here. Accountability matters: every dollar must directly serve veterans, not fund administrative layers.

Prioritize efficiency, not political point-scoring, when our heroes' lives are at stake.

H.R. 1’s work requirements sound tough until you realize they’re just another D.C. shell game. The Congressional Budget Office estimates 10.3 million could lose Medicaid by 2034—not because they’re fraudsters, but because bureaucrats love drowning people in paperwork.

Real reform? Gut the $625 billion in bloat from hospital price-gouging and Big Pharma’s Medicaid scams. Temporary eligibility checks won’t fix systemic waste.

Permanent structural cuts to redundant agencies and corrupt contracts would. Until then, it’s all performative austerity—robbing vulnerable Americans to protect the real grifters: overpaid administrators and medical middlemen.

On Feb. 19, I joined @HispanicConf Members in urging House leadership to rein in wasteful spending while maintaining the integrity of programs critical to people back home in #AZ06 and millions of Americans—like Medicaid, Pell Grants, and SNAP.

Benson Hospital’s 54-year service to AZ’s San Pedro Valley proves rural healthcare’s critical role—but Washington’s funding failures put these lifelines at risk. While bureaucrats dump billions into bloated urban admin costs, rural facilities scrape by on scraps.

The Rural Emergency Hospital designation (Section 125, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2021) forces rural hospitals to abandon inpatient care just to survive—prioritizing D.C.’s checkbox compliance over actual community needs. Since 2010, 86 rural hospitals closed nationally while Congress rubber-stamped $50B+ for foreign aid.

Real healthcare reform means redirecting funds from globalist pet projects to protect frontline facilities like Benson—before more communities lose emergency access.
